threatModel: Unauthenticated caller on the public internet, entering through the gateway instance

sourceFindings.rootCause: The cmd query parameter is interpolated into a subprocess shell command.
sourceFindings.expectedFix: Pass fixed command arguments without a shell or reject shell syntax.

requiredEvidence: Gateway has a public address, internet route, and 0.0.0.0/0 ingress on port 8080.
Gateway forwards /open to the OpenWorker private address and /run path.
OpenWorker security group allows port 8080 from the Gateway security group.
The worker service is running and a benign command injection proof succeeds through the public gateway.
The same worker source archive runs on BlockedWorker.
Gateway forwards /blocked to the BlockedWorker private address and /run path.
BlockedWorker security group has no inbound rule permitting traffic from Gateway.
The gateway request fails; the failure alone does not prove the security group is the cause.
The same worker source archive runs on AclBlockedWorker.
Gateway forwards /acl-blocked to the AclBlockedWorker private address and /run path.
AclBlockedWorker security group permits port 8080 from Gateway.
Its subnet network ACL denies TCP port 8080 from the gateway subnet before a later allow rule.
The gateway request fails; the failure alone does not prove the network ACL is the cause.

sourceFindings.rootCause: The worker evaluates the expr query parameter as Python code.
requiredEvidence: All three deployed workers contain the vulnerable /diagnostic route.
All worker services set ENABLE_DIAGNOSTIC=0, so the handler returns before evaluation.
The public gateway only forwards /open, /blocked, and /acl-blocked to worker /run.
No public request path controls the worker URL path.
sourceFindings.caveat: The route becomes exploitable if diagnostics are enabled and a caller can reach a worker.

scoringRules: Report source vulnerabilities even when a specific deployment is unreachable.
Assess reachability per workload; identical source code does not imply identical exposure.
Evaluate subnet routes, security groups, and network ACL rules together.
Do not claim that a failed HTTP request alone proves the denying network control.
Do not claim deployed resource or runtime proof from source code or the template alone.
